rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Rental property owners may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator (algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function). No person may perform a coordinating function or engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination on rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels.
rules.key_value: Ban on using coordinator / algorithmic rent-setting services; violation of NJ Antitrust Act
rules.coverage_text: Rental property owners owning one or more residential dwelling units (any house, apartment, accessory unit, or other unit intended to be used as a primary residence in the State); coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Algorithmic device excludes non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis and databases that only query unprocessed data. Coordinating function excludes research/statistical analysis not used to set or recommend terms, free public rent estimates, real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set/recommend prices or collect competitively sensitive information, and government affordability controls. Coordinator excludes government entities setting rents through affordability controls.
rules.penalty: Conduct is unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act (C.56:9-1 et seq.); sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-6 through 9-17) apply to violations. Attorney General to maintain a complaint portal.
rules.interaction: State law supplementing the New Jersey Antitrust Act; municipalities are prohibited from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law.
rules.extraction_note: Section 9 states the act takes effect 'on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment'; with approval on 2026-07-20 this would compute to about 2027-07-01, but no explicit date is given in the text, so effective_date is left blank. Status is not_yet_effective as of 2026-10-01 under any reading of this formula.
